subject: Model fit follow-up: benchmark links, prompt set, and rollback trigger criteria
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@velocitypay.com>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@payway.io>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — model recommendations and next steps

Thanks again for a great call this morning, Claire — quick recap + concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap (30m call):
- Primary goal: Replace rule-based customer support triage with ML-assisted intent classification + suggested responses for top 8 intents.
- Current constraints: strict latency target <= 120ms p50, sensitive PII redaction, need audit trail for classifications.

Redwood fit / model recs: 
- Recommended serving candidates: redwood/fastchat-7b-q4 (balanced latency/cost), redwood/claify-13b-fp16 (higher accuracy for complex intents)
- We'll provide an eval pack (benchmark suite + golden prompts) so you can compare both on your data.

What I'm delivering by EOD Thursday (May 11):
- Eval pack link (sample prompts + metrics): prompt_set_v1.csv (attached)
- Benchmarks summary link: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/velocitypay-benchmarks-2028
- Suggested pin/rollback criteria (draft): see bullets below — want your buy-in.

Suggested rollback / pin triggers (draft):
- Regressions on your golden set: > 5 percentage point drop in intent accuracy vs pinned baseline
- Hallucination rate increase: > 3x on targeted hallucination checks
- Observed model latency p50 increase > 20% after deploy (measured under same traffic profile)
- Any verified privacy/data-leak finding during evaluation or initial rollout

If any trigger fires, automatic fallback -> pinned variant + on-call notification; if persistent, we snapshot artifacts and open a rollback event with your ops team.

Ask from you:
1) Confirm these trigger thresholds look reasonable for VelocityPay (yes/no or adjustments)
2) Confirm we can share the eval pack with Rajesh and his team for their tests
3) If you want, we can arrange a short technical sync Wed 10–11am PT to align on measurement instruments.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.csv

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Claire Wu <claire.wu@velocitypay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@payway.io>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — model recommendations and next steps

Thanks, Dylan — useful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

- On the rollback triggers: is the 5pp drop measured on a small golden set or a larger sampled validation set? We need to make sure noise doesn't trigger a rollback.
- Hallucination metric — can you share the exact check we run? Rajesh will want to reproduce locally.
- If we pin to a model version, how do we handle infra patches (kernel/quant changes) that might still cause behavior diffs?

We can take the eval pack — please share with Rajesh. Also, security wants to see your audit log and model artifact snapshot process before any production rollout. Looping Rajesh here for availability; he prefers Wed 10:00am PT.

— Claire
Head of Product Operations | VelocityPay

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Wu <claire.wu@velocitypay.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@payway.io>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — model recommendations and next steps

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Claire's questions so we can finalize the thresholds and artifacts. Quick internal proposal below (I'll send to Claire after you ack):

Proposal for measuring triggers (internal draft):
- Golden set: 1,200 labeled examples pulled from VelocityPay historical tickets (stratified by intent). Use this for accuracy/regression tests; require a minimum sample size to avoid noisy flips.
- Statistical test: two-sided binomial test with alpha=0.01 for accuracy change; require both absolute >5pp and statistically significant to trigger automated rollback.
- Hallucination check: 300 targeted hallucination prompts based on historical failure modes; define hallucination as hallucination_score >= 0.7 (Redwood's internal detector). Trigger if false-positive rate increases by 3x AND the change passes bootstrap significance.
- Latency measurement: use our synthetic load harness reproducing your median request size; p50 baseline measured over 10,000 inferences. Trigger if p50 increases >20% sustained for 30 minutes.
- Infra/abi changes: if a kernel/quantization patch occurs and behavior changes but passes metrics, mark as an "infra diff" — require a canary and explicit artifact snapshot.

Pinning / snapshot workflow (draft):
1) If trigger fires -> immediately route production traffic to pinned snapshot (customer-facing pin) and open an incident.
2) We create an artifact bundle (model weights checksum, serving runtime version, quantization metadata, KV cache format, Docker image tag) and upload to customer-controlled S3 escrow (we provide manifest).
3) If customer requests rollback, we deploy the snapshot, run quick smoke checks, then lift the fallback.

Attachments: diff_report_summary.pdf (high-level sample diff we showed on call)

Action items: 
- Marissa: prepare the eval pack and golden set sampling plan by EOD Wed (May 10) — include test harness reproducible script and expected metrics report.
- Aditya: confirm the artifact manifest fields we include for escrow and any KMS/HSM integration notes.

I plan to send the updated thresholds to Claire after you both ack.

— Dylan
